_: Tile pack manifest. THE swap point: point `sheets` elsewhere and rewrite `tiles` to use different art with no code change.
_provenance: `tiles` and `decor` are reference art only — a 1-bit dungeon set dropped into inbox/, not licensed for release; placeholder until replaced or cleared. `paramyth` is the project's own art (DJ, from 2026-09-25) and ships.
_semantics: Labelled by DJ 2026-09-22 in the Barrowlands Tileset Legend artifact, replacing an earlier guess. tiles: c1-c3 x r1-r3 is a nine-slice wall set (outer corners, edges, centre) with c4-c5 r1-r2 as extra pieces, probably inner corners; wall sets repeat at c7-c11 r1-r3 and c1-c11 r5-r8 (set C extends to c4-c5 r8). The clusters at c1-c4 and c7-c9 r9-r11 are ORNATE FLOOR sets, not walls. c14-c16 r1-r3 plain slabs, r4-r6 paving stones (r7 blank). c18-c20 r1-r3 angular/lattice floor, r4-r7 brick, cobble, checker. c13-c19 r9-r12 elaborate architecture, unused. decor (objects, over a floor): c1-c3 r1-r2 misc blocks (c3 r2 is an inverted square pit), r3 rocks, r4 table/chair/POT (called a crate 2026-09-22 and corrected 2026-09-22: the sprite is a round-bellied pot, and there is no crate on either sheet), r5-r6 urns/barrels/sacks, c2 r6 is a BOTTLE, not a sack (DJ, 2026-09-22) and is unused for now; c1-c2 r7 STAIRS DOWN (left and right), c1-c2 r8 STAIRS UP, c3 r7-r8 ladders, c1-c2 r9-r12 banners, c3 r9-r12 unidentified (do not use). c4: r1 grate, r2 closed chest, r3 open chest, r4 spikes, r5-r6 crystals. c5: r1 skeleton (inert), r2 key, r3 square gem, r4 misc item, r5 lever.
_gaps: PILLAR is gone: there is no pillar art on either sheet, and pointing it at the nine-slice's interior fill drew a featureless block in the middle of rooms (DJ spotted it 2026-09-22). Archetypes now place 2x2 WALL, which the nine-slice renders as four outer corners. NICHE still has no real answer and borrows the grate at decor 4,1; it at least has detail. If the unlabelled architecture block at tiles c13-c19 r9-12 turns out to hold columns, pillars could become a type again with real art.
name: 1-bit dungeon (reference)
_shade: Optional per-type multiplier on the stratum pair, toward black. Two-tone art cannot differ in value on its own, so this is what makes wall read apart from floor: floor sits dark and walkable, wall stone takes the light. WALKABLE tiles share the floor's value: the stairs sat at the wall's 1.0 and read as a bright block pasted over the floor (DJ, 2026-09-22). A gate holds them equal now.
_kinds: variants = pick one cell from its own coordinates. nineslice = pick from a 3x3 block by which orthogonal neighbours share the type; origin is the block's top-left. overlay = draw `base` first, then a cell on top.

WALL._inner: Offsets from origin. The extra cells at c4-c5 r1-r2 each carry a solid light quadrant in one corner; that quadrant points at the diagonal where the floor is.

SARC._: Full-bleed masonry, so it is not an overlay: it covered its FLOOR base completely and the base was a wasted draw. It keeps the wall's value because a sarcophagus is stone standing up, not floor.

STAIR_D._: A fixed pale stone at full value. Pulled down to the floor's 0.42 to stop it reading as a bright block pasted on the ground, which worked and then made it nearly invisible (DJ, 2026-09-22). Its own tone solves both: bright enough to find, dark half kept dark so a descent still reads as a hole, and the same at every depth so a staircase looks like a staircase wherever you meet it.

STAIR_U._: A fixed pale stone at full value. Pulled down to the floor's 0.42 to stop it reading as a bright block pasted on the ground, which worked and then made it nearly invisible (DJ, 2026-09-22). Its own tone solves both: bright enough to find, dark half kept dark so a descent still reads as a hole, and the same at every depth so a staircase looks like a staircase wherever you meet it.

player._: A glyph, not a sprite. The reference sheet's character did not fit the tone. Swap to a sprite by replacing this with { sheet, w, h, idle, walk }.

_items: Item art, keyed by the kinds in core/items.js. `cells` are variants; a container may also declare `opened`. Items draw at full shade so loot reads against the dark floor.

chest._: Banded gold. The art's light half becomes bright yellow, which is what makes a chest read as the thing worth crossing a room for.

barrel._: Wood. A fixed tone, so it is the same timber at every depth — the stratum remap is for architecture, not for objects.

table._: Wood. A fixed tone, so it is the same timber at every depth — the stratum remap is for architecture, not for objects.

chair._: Wood. A fixed tone, so it is the same timber at every depth — the stratum remap is for architecture, not for objects.

bcap._: Blasting Cap; B.Cap in the UI. DJ's bomb, own art, cell 1.
bcap._tone: iron. A fixed tone wins over the stratum: a bomb is the same bomb at every depth.

_foes: Enemies, keyed by the kinds in core/foes.js. A glyph, like the player, because the reference sheet's characters do not fit the tone either. Swap to a sprite by replacing this with { sheet, w, h, idle, walk }.

dog._pop: rot-red (palette.rot): what a rot-touched thing is full of

sentinel._: lichen on old stone (palette.lichen): a statue that moves

glazes._: Glazes, by stratum. Pottery is not one colour the way timber is: it is whatever it was dipped in, and which glazes existed depends on where and when it was fired. A piece keeps its glaze wherever you carry it, chosen from its OWN address — so an imperial cobalt urn stays cobalt among surface terracotta, which is exactly the tell design/world-shape.md wants.

_stations: Camp stations. PLACEHOLDER art borrowed from decor: there are no NPCs or counters on this sheet.

stash._: The same chest sprite as the item, so the same banded gold.

_sheets_note: `paramyth` is the project's OWN sheet, built from paramyth-20.txt by tools/build-sheet.mjs. 20px cells, the pack's two-tone palette, transparent ground. 0 sword (DJ), 1 blasting cap (DJ).

scar._: Where furniture was blasted. A DECAL, not a tile type: drawn over the floor from s.scars in its own pass. Placeholder: the rubble scatter, dimmer than rubble so it reads as debris and not a rock. Own art wanted.
